newsitem.title: CHILE: Lower grades cut Codelco molybdenum output.
newsitem.headline: Lower grades cut Codelco molybdenum output.

text.p: Lower metal grades at the Chuquicamata pit will cut state copper company Codelco's molybdenum output to about 30 million pounds this year from 37 million in 1995, a senior Codelco official said.
Molybdenum grades have been lower than usual for about a year at Chuquicamata but have shown an especially strong drop in the last three months, said the official.

"Like any producer, we have ups and downs in our grades. And in the last three months or so, we've been the below the normal range in molybdenum grades at Chuqui," he said. Codelco officials rarely speak on the record.
Codelco produced about 37 million pounds of the copper subproduct last year, about 22 million of that from Chuquicamata and the rest divided between Codelco's three other mines, said the official.
Production this year will slip to about 30 million pounds, with almost all the reduction at Chuquicamata, he said.
"Our normal production is about 35 million to 30 million pounds, so we're still in the normal range but on the low end of it," he said.
Molybdenum is extracted from copper in the concentrator plants, which have had no mechanical problems affecting output, he said. "The problem is entirely in the mineral grades," he said.
Codelco geologists were unsure how long the drop would last, he said, adding, "That's the one question they can't answer for me."
